x: George Hoath, our L.F.F. member, has again been supreme over Ten Miles, winning at Reading and Bexleyheath. Harry Parker, in addition to the donkey work of being Hon.

Tom Carter and Gosney (Eastleigh) soon sorted themselves out, followed by George Hoath and took the field along at a rare pace and these places were maintained to the finish, although Tom made a game effort.

Championship, held in conjunction Tom Carter retained his title in 27.23, beating the course record, held by George Hoath, by 10secs. Bert Mitchell gained fourth prize, Dick Tobin was 6th and Tom Morrell 7th.

Tom Carter ran well to finish 2nd, and George Hoath was 3rd. With Len Herbert 6th and Tom Morrell 8th we scored an easy win in the team championship, an honour which we have secured in 1925, 1926, 1929, 1930, 1931, 1933, 1934, 1935, 1936 and 1937.

Tom Clinton ran very well to hand over in second place and George Hoath, running for our "B" team, was in third place. Both our "C" and "D" teams were also well up and we were the only club to field and, what is more important, close in four complete teams.
